La temperatura siempre en kelvin (T = t: Temperature always in kelvin (T = t + 273.15). At standard conditions (1 atm and 0 °C) one mole occupies 22.4 L. The density of a gas is $ρ = PM/(RT)$.
$ΔU = Q − W$, &ensp; $ΔU = n C_v ΔT$, &e: $ΔU = Q − W$,   $ΔU = n C_v ΔT$,   $C_p − C_v = R$,   $γ = C_p/C_v$
W es el trabajo que hace el gas (positiv: W is the work done by the gas (positive if it expands) and Q the heat it receives. A monatomic gas has $C_v = {3}/{2} R$ and a diatomic one $C_v = {5}/{2} R$.
<b>Isoterma</b> (T constante): $ΔU = 0$: Isothermal (constant T): $ΔU = 0$ and $Q = W = nRT ln {V_2}/{V_1}$. Isobaric (constant P): $W = P ΔV$ and $Q = n C_p ΔT$. Isochoric (constant V): $W = 0$ and $Q = n C_v ΔT$. Adiabatic (Q = 0): $P V^γ$ = const, $T V^{γ − 1}$ = const and $W = {P_1 V_1 − P_2 V_2}/{γ − 1}$.
En un ciclo el gas vuelve al estado inic: In a cycle the gas returns to its initial state, so $ΔU = 0$ and $W_{net} = Q_{net}$, which is the area enclosed in the P-V diagram. The efficiency is $η = W/Q_{abs}$, and it never exceeds that of a Carnot cycle between the same temperatures, $η = 1 − T_c/T_h$. The named cycles (Carnot, Otto, Diesel, Brayton, Stirling) and the T-S diagram are in Thermodynamic cycles.
En una mezcla de gases ideales cada uno: In a mixture of ideal gases each one behaves as if it were alone in the whole container. Its partial pressure is $P_i = x_i P$, with $x_i = n_i/n$ its mole fraction, and the total pressure is the sum of the partial pressures (Dalton's law).
La ecuación de Van der Waals corrige el: The Van der Waals equation corrects the ideal gas: b is the volume of the molecules themselves and a measures how much they attract each other. The compressibility factor $Z = PV/(nRT)$ is 1 for an ideal gas. Above the critical temperature, $T_c = 8a/(27Rb)$, the gas cannot be liquefied.
La ecuación de Redlich-Kwong, $P = {RT}/: The Redlich–Kwong equation, $P = {RT}/{V_m − b} − {a}/{√T V_m (V_m + b)}$, with $a = 0.42748 R^2 T_c^{2.5}/P_c$ and $b = 0.08664 R T_c/P_c$, depends on the critical temperature and critical pressure (here those from Van der Waals). It fits better than Van der Waals at high pressures; the graph of Z against P compares them with the ideal gas (Z = 1).
Las velocidades de las moléculas siguen: The speeds of the molecules follow the Maxwell distribution: the most probable is $√(2RT/M)$ and the mean $√(8RT/(πM))$. The mean kinetic energy depends only on temperature. Between collisions a molecule travels on average $λ = 1/(√2 π d^2 n_V)$, with d its diameter and $n_V = P/(kT)$ the molecules per cubic metre.
Redlich-Kwong usa los mismos Tc y Pc que: Redlich–Kwong uses the same Tc and Pc as Van der Waals (derived from a and b), not tabulated critical values: it is a comparison of models, not experimental data for the gas.
Los modelos de gas real solo valen en la: The real-gas models only hold in the single-phase region: near the critical point or inside the condensation region the results stop being reliable.
